extraction.Name: Jennie M. Coates, nee Cummings
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not desire the patent to her 160 acre allotment, when it was issued in September, 1919, but that the Indian Agency informed her that her land would be assessed for taxes, for which it would later be sold, if she did not take the patent and pay the taxes, so she accepted the patent
extraction.Buyer: Mortgaged to Bellas-Hess, of Omaha, Nebraska, for $1200.00; sold in 1922 to Mrs. Dorothy Snyder, of Martin, South Dakota, Mrs. Snyder assuming the mortgage and paying the taxes that had accumulated after the mortgage was made; Mrs. Snyder traded her a livery barn, valued at $1000.00, on the deal
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: got behind in taxes on her quarter, and, in 1921, she mortgaged her land to Bellas-Hess, of Omaha, Nebraska, for $1200.00; that she did not make payments on this loan, and, in 1922, she sold the allotment
extraction.Occupation/Income: her husband farms for a living; and that is his only income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; has pretty good health; husband has good health and supports her and her six children; did not sell her place for debts incurred prior to receiving her patent in fee; the $1200.00 she borrowed all went into the place in the way of lumber and taxes; the livery barn did not prove to be a money maker; considers she got a poor deal out of her place; has never received any aid from the County, State nor the United States Government; document sworn December 27, 1928; County of Shannon, State of South Dakota
